Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

grief noun

also mourning, mourn, feel grief, get over (grief), sorrow, grieve

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.18 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 153, 156
Cic. Tusc. 4.18: maeror est aegritūdō flēbilis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 324

maeror, maerōris m.

noun, third declension

grief, mourning, sorrow

Grief that weeps and shows itself: Cicero defines it as a tearful sorrow.

Other words

  • lūgeō, lūgēre, lūxī, lūctum — to mourn

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 156

  • condolēscō, condolēscere, condoluī — to feel pain, grieve

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 153; Plaut. Truc. 2.8.2: mihi … condoluit caput (Lewis & Short); Traupman 324

    Lewis & Short gives it of physical pain above all (dēns, pēs condoluit); of grief it is less common.

  • superō, superāre, superāvī, superātum — to get over, overcome (grief, anger)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 153

  • dolor, dolōris m. — pain, grief

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

    Pain of body or mind; Cicero sets the two side by side: maerōrem minuī; dolōrem nec potuī (Att. 12.28.2, Lewis & Short s.v. maeror).

  • luctus, luctūs m. — mourning (for the dead)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical

See also sadness, sad, recover.
